$comment: Color tokens map 1:1 to --kavacha-* CSS custom properties on the chrome root.
$readBeforeEditing: EDITING THIS FILE DOES NOT CHANGE THE BROWSER. It is the reference copy of
the default theme, not its source. Midnight is the BAKED default: patch 0016
%includes its tokens into zen-theme.css at build time, and KavachaThemeEngine
deliberately clears all overrides when the active theme is the default, so
that build-time floor is what you actually see (that early return is what
makes the default look flash-free -- it is a feature, not an oversight).
style.css beside this file is inert for the same reason: built-in themes are
colors-only, and the engine loads a package style.css only for user themes.
So this package has three consumers, none of which is the running default:
1. Documentation -- the reference implementation of the package format.
2. A starting point to copy into the profile's kavacha-themes/<id>/, where
it IS live and every token below takes effect.
3. Nothing else. The shipped default reads none of it.
To actually change the default look you must edit BOTH real sources:
src/zen/kavacha-theme/kavacha-midnight.inc.css   (patch 0016, baked floor)
BUILTIN_THEMES['kavacha-midnight'] in KavachaThemeEngine.sys.mjs
and then mirror the change here. Recorded as defect D5 (resolved as
not-a-bug, kept as a maintenance trap); see documentation/REMAINING_WORK.md.
The baked floor carries only surface/text/border. The remaining tokens here
(tab*, sidebar*, urlbar*, success/warning/danger/privacyShield, textDisabled
and the accent trio) are NOT baked, and take effect only for user themes.
accent* in particular is intentionally absent from the default: Kavacha ships
no default accent (2026-07-13) and the welcome flow asks. Chrome that needs a
colour before the user has answered uses --kavacha-accent-fallback.
